titel: What Is The Net Worth Of The World

einzeiler: Why surging global net worth and asset prices without productivity growth spell trouble.
kurzfassung: The world's total net worth has reached about 600 trillion US dollars, significantly outpacing global GDP growth since the year 2000. This massive expansion is primarily driven by rising asset prices and debt rather than actual productive value creation. Experts warn that this growing disconnect between paper wealth and real economic output risks a major financial reset unless productivity catches up.
stichpunkte: Global net worth has reached approximately 600 trillion dollars, quadrupling since 2000 and growing twice as fast as global GDP.
Gross Domestic Product measures economic flow, while a balance sheet reveals true net worth and financial strength.
Real estate accounts for over two thirds of all real global assets, while intellectual property makes up less than 5%.
Households own roughly 95% of the world's total wealth, heavily concentrated in the top 1 percent.
Since 2001, 75 percent of net worth growth has been driven by price increases rather than new investment.
For every dollar of new investment generated over the last 25 years, the global economy has produced two dollars of debt.
Stock market valuations often reflect paper transactions and market sentiment rather than underlying business growth.
Proposed policy solutions to encourage productive investment include land value taxes, vacant property levies, and wealth taxes.

clips.hook: Determining global net worth based on assumptions
clips.text: Calculating worldwide wealth relies heavily on subjective valuations and educated guesses rather than clear paper trails, especially when evaluating intangible assets.
Despite massive technological advancements and artificial intelligence breakthroughs, physical land and built structures make up nearly seventy percent of all real assets.

clips.hook: Price increases drive net worth growth
clips.text: The vast majority of wealth expansion over the last two decades stems from rising valuations rather than inflation or productive investments.
Instead of reinvesting profits into tools that boost output, major companies spend trillions purchasing their own stock to artificially inflate market prices.

clips.hook: Using taxes to change economic incentives
clips.text: Policy tools like land value taxes can discourage the hoarding of empty property and force capital into productive economic uses.
